project_specification.project_name: nullius — feature 323 (System exposes POST /risk/halt, which flattens open positions and rejects new order submission)
project_specification.addition_summary:
Implement app_spec.xml feature 323 in the existing risk member (packages/risk, import name risk; seat src/app/modules/risk): a *halt door*, `POST /risk/halt`, that flattens open positions and rejects new order submission. This is the composed act the category was built for — the one place where feature 322's kill channel and feature 330's flatten are driven in order, over the same shared relational store, so that a single instruction both stops the source and drains the sink. Feature 323 depends on feature 322 (the channel that carries the standing kill instruction) and presupposes feature 330 (the flatten that survives a hung strategy process): the door sends the kill through 322's channel, then drives 330's flatten over the book, and the two cannot be separated because a flatten without the kill first on record is refused by the flatten's own authority check, and a kill that does not flatten leaves the exposure standing. The member already holds every piece the door composes — the kill channel (risk.kill: RiskKillSwitch, send_kill, require_orders_allowed, KILL_INSTRUCTION), the flattener (risk.flatten: RiskFlattener, flatten_positions, FlattenResult, FLATTEN_STATUS_COMPLETED) and the error taxonomy (risk.errors) — so feature 323 adds no new table, no new kill, no new flatten verb and no new error class: it is the seam that sends and flattens in order, and the endpoint that serves it.
The endpoint is a Python seam, not an HTTP server — exactly the stance the forward member (POST /forward/promote, feature 332) and the ledger member (POST /ledger/debit, feature 95) take. It holds a kill switch and a flattener, both resolved over the same DATABASE_URL, and its one verb, `post(request)`, drives them in the order the sentence names: send the kill (322's first-write-wins send, which lands the standing instruction and returns the record), then flatten the book (330's engine-judged flatten, which cancels every order and closes every position and returns only a completed result). The rejection of new order submission is not a second act the door performs — it is the *consequence* of the kill it just sent: the order layer's submission path already consults risk.require_orders_allowed (feature 322's guard), which raises RiskOrdersKilledError while the instruction stands, so once the door has sent the kill the order layer is refused by the channel that already exists. The door does not reach into the order path to enforce anything; it sets the state the order path already refuses under, and the separation is the feature — the halt door is the supervisor's verb, the guard is the order layer's read, and the shared row between them is what makes "rejects new order submission" true without the door holding any authority of its own.
The endpoint is registered as a component beside the switch and the ledger, following the ledger member's precedent (ledger-debit, ledger-k-effective register their endpoints beside the store) rather than the forward member's (which leaves its endpoint as a function of the store). The halt endpoint holds two resolved objects — the switch and the flattener — over one URL, and a composed application that carries the halt door must carry both pointed at the same database; registering it under its own name keeps that object graph to one component the caller asks for by name, rather than a pair the caller would have to keep consistent. The member's existing three components (risk, risk-halt-events, risk-flattener) are untouched; the door adds a fourth, `risk-halt`. The door sends through the module-level `risk.send_kill` and drives through `risk.flatten_positions`'s underlying store, resolving the same DATABASE_URL the switch and flattener were built from, so the four doors cannot disagree. No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings or migration is edited; the member joins by workspace-scan convention and imports no other workspace member.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace (packages/* members, import names are underscored slugs) / pytest (ruff + mypy conventions). The module loader discovers members from the root pyproject.toml `[tool.uv.workspace] members = ["packages/*"]`, imports each package so its module-level `@register` fires, and composes what each `@register` builder contributes under a component name. `app` (src/app) is a namespace package with no `__init__.py`; the seats in src/app/modules/<member>/ are reached by namespace import (e.g. app.modules.risk, app.modules.router). A member never imports another member — it reaches shared shapes through `app.*`, never through a sibling package's import name.
existing_context.test_baseline: The repository-level suite under tests/ is collected by pytest with testpaths=tests; each workspace member's own suite lives under packages/<member>/tests/ and is collected under its own conftest (same-basename files collide under one pytest run), and is NOT graded by the bare `uv run pytest` acceptance gate — a member suite must be run explicitly (run both `uv run pytest tests/` and the member's own `packages/risk/tests/`). Feature 323 composes two acts the member already owns (send + flatten) over the shared relational store, so it adds no third-party dependency: stdlib sqlite3, frozen dataclasses, no I/O beyond the store the channel and flatten already touch. Measure the real numbers by running the suite before relying on them. The repo lint is red on main (mypy absent, pre-existing ruff errors), so lint only the changed files and compare to a sibling.
existing_context.conventions: snake_case modules, frozen dataclasses for value types, docstrings that cite app_spec.xml feature numbers and docs/alpha-engine-prd.md / docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md sections, stdlib-only computation, `@register` only in the package `__init__` (never a submodule — a submodule's registration fires only on the first `create_app()` of a process), degrade-don't-break composition (a builder that raises would take composition down for every unrelated feature, so a builder returns `None` for a deployment that names no store), member-owned tables created lazily beside the only module that writes them (never in the shared migration chain, which is order-sensitive and excluded from this feature's file claim), and the error-vocabulary discipline that no member imports another and a shared helper that raises another feature's error type defeats the caller's `except` (translate at the seam). The risk member already lives in this workspace (packages/risk: the kill channel feature 322, the flatten feature 330, the halt event ledger feature 331, and the `__init__` that re-exports and fires `@register("risk")`, `@register("risk-halt-events")`, `@register("risk-flattener")`, seat src/app/modules/risk). Feature 323 is a sibling within that member, not a new member. The governing documents are docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md §13.3 ("Runs as a separate process with kill authority over the execution engine, so a hung strategy process cannot prevent a flatten"), §17 ("No inbound ports on the live trading host" — the endpoint is a Python seam, never a served socket), and docs/alpha-engine-prd.md C10 ("Risk and kill switches").

category.name: Risk Supervisor & Kill Switches
category.feature: System exposes POST /risk/halt, which flattens open positions and rejects new order submission.

project_specification.integration_points:
The halt door is the composed act of feature 322's kill channel and feature 330's flatten, served at `POST /risk/halt` as a Python seam over the risk member. It is reached directly from the member (`from risk import RiskHaltEndpoint, HaltRequest, HaltResponse, RISK_HALT_ROUTE`), the way feature 322's `send_kill` and feature 330's `flatten_positions` are, and — for a composed application — through the new seat accessor in src/app/modules/risk, which already hands back the switch (risk), the halt event ledger (risk-halt-events) and the flattener (risk-flattener); feature 323 adds one component, `risk-halt`, and one accessor, `halt_component`, reached the same way.
The endpoint holds a kill switch and a flattener, both resolved over the same DATABASE_URL at construction (`HaltEndpoint.from_env` resolves both exactly as the member's own builders do, so the endpoint and the composed components always point at the same database; no DATABASE_URL composes no endpoint — an unconfigured store is a discoverable state, not an error). It is duck-checked against the seams it drives, not isinstance-guarded, because the factory's scan imports the member under an alias module so the composed switch and flattener are structurally the right shape but never the same class object a direct import yields.
The endpoint's one verb, `post(request)`, drives the two acts in the order the sentence names. First the kill: the endpoint sends feature 322's kill instruction through the switch it holds (`RiskKillSwitch.send`, first-write- wins — a halt over an already-killed channel writes nothing and returns the standing record with `changed=False`), so the standing instruction lands on record. Then the flatten: the endpoint drives feature 330's flatten over the book (`RiskFlattener.flatten` with a caller-supplied execution engine face), which reads the standing kill it just sent (the authority check passes, because the send wrote the row first-write-wins and the flatten reads it back), cancels every order standing, closes every position open, and returns only a completed result — an engine whose own re-reading reports nothing standing. The flatten's refusal (a residue, a fault, an engine that cannot be asked) propagates as `RiskFlattenError`; the kill's refusal (a bad ask, a store that cannot take the row) propagates as `RiskKillSwitchError` / `RiskStoreError`. The endpoint composes neither act's vocabulary — it propagates the channel's and the flatten's own refusals, exactly as the forward endpoint propagates the store's and the promotion's.
The rejection of new order submission is the *consequence* of the kill the door sends, not a third act: the order layer's submission path already consults `risk.require_orders_allowed` (feature 322's guard), which raises `RiskOrdersKilledError` carrying the standing instruction while one stands, so once the door has sent the kill the order layer is refused by the channel that already exists. The door does not reach into the order path, does not hold order authority, and does not enforce anything itself — it sets the state the order path already refuses under, and the shared row between the send and the guard is what makes "rejects new order submission" true. The caller wires the endpoint into the order path at the single point where a halt must be pronounced: it constructs the endpoint (or asks the seat for the `risk-halt` component), builds a `HaltRequest` carrying the execution engine it holds, and calls `post`; on the completed `HaltResponse` the order layer is already killed and the book is already flat, and every later submission the guard refuses is the door's work standing.
The request carries the execution engine face the flatten must drive — the one thing no composition can supply, because it is the supervisor's own hold on the execution engine (feature 330's law: kill authority is a process's fact, not an application's). There is no request body beyond the engine: the kill's moment defaults to the instant of the call and the sender to the calling process's kernel-read identity, exactly as `risk.send_kill` and `risk.flatten_positions` refuse a caller-supplied label, so a halt cannot borrow another process's name. The response carries the standing kill instruction the door sent (which process killed, and when — first-write- wins, so a retry over an already-killed channel returns the first record) and the completed flatten result (what was cancelled, what was closed, when it completed), so the caller holds the record of both acts rather than a re-derivation.
project_specification.constraints: - Feature 323 is the *composed act* of feature 322's kill and feature 330's flatten, served at `POST /risk/halt`. It must NOT add a new table, a new kill, a new flatten verb, or a new error class: it sends through `risk.send_kill` / `RiskKillSwitch.send`, flattens through `risk.flatten_positions` / `RiskFlattener.flatten`, and propagates the channel's and flatten's own refusals (`RiskKillSwitchError`, `RiskStoreError`, `RiskFlattenError`, `RiskOrdersKilledError`) unchanged. Feature 322's and feature 330's existing behaviour, messages, codes and tests must be untouched. - The endpoint is a Python seam, never an HTTP server: it holds no socket, serves no port and imports no HTTP framework, per docs/nullius-tech- architecture.md §17 ("No inbound ports on the live trading host"). The route is spelled once as `RISK_HALT_ROUTE = "/risk/halt"`, pinned as a class attribute so `HaltEndpoint.route` states the contract without an instance, matching the forward and ledger members' `route` convention. - The endpoint drives the two acts in the order the sentence names: send the kill first (so the standing instruction is on record), then flatten (so the flatten's authority check passes). It must not flatten before sending, because a flatten under no standing kill is refused by the flatten's own authority check, and it must not send after flattening, because the kill stops the source the flatten drains. - The rejection of new order submission is the consequence of the kill, not a separate enforcement: the endpoint sets the standing instruction and the order layer's existing `risk.require_orders_allowed` guard (feature 322) refuses under it. The endpoint must not reach into the order path, hold order authority, or enforce the refusal itself. - The request carries the execution engine face (the supervisor's own hold on the engine, caller-supplied and duck-checked, never composed) and nothing else: no caller-supplied kill moment, no caller-supplied sender label (both default to the instant and the kernel-read identity, as 322 and 330 refuse), no observation fields. A `HaltRequest` is a frozen value carrying exactly the engine. - The response is a frozen value carrying the standing kill instruction the door sent (first-write-wins, so a retry returns the first record) and the completed flatten result (what was cancelled and closed, when it completed), so the caller holds the record of both acts. - `@register` lives only in the package `__init__`, never a submodule. The endpoint registers as one new component, `risk-halt`, beside the member's existing three (`risk`, `risk-halt-events`, `risk-flattener`), which are untouched. The seat src/app/modules/risk adds one accessor, `halt_component`, reached the same way as the existing three. - No member imports another. The endpoint resolves its switch and flattener from DATABASE_URL exactly as the member's own builders do, so the four doors cannot disagree; it imports no sibling member. - No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings or migration is edited. No order-sensitive shared file is edited (the order-sensitive shared files are excluded from this feature's file claim entirely). - Degrade-don't-break composition: the `risk-halt` builder returns `None` when no DATABASE_URL is configured (an unconfigured store is a discoverable state, not an error), so a composed application without a store composes no halt endpoint rather than breaking. - The refusal message vocabulary is inherited, not restated: a bad kill ask raises in `RiskKillSwitchError` (opening `kill_instruction`), a store that cannot take the row in `RiskStoreError`, a residue or engine fault in `RiskFlattenError` (opening `flatten`). The endpoint composes no message of its own. - All existing tests in the risk member (packages/risk/tests) and in tests/ must stay green. The member's own suite must be run explicitly (it is not graded by the bare `uv run pytest` gate).

implementation_steps.step: Phase 1 — the request, the response and the route constant. Add one new module, `packages/risk/src/risk/halt.py`. (1) Add `RISK_HALT_ROUTE = "/risk/halt"`, the one route the endpoint serves, pinned so the endpoint, the spec's API summary and whatever routes the deployment match on one spelling. (2) Add a `HaltRequest` frozen value carrying exactly the execution engine face it must drive — the supervisor's own hold, caller-supplied and duck-checked, never composed, with no caller-supplied kill moment or sender label (both default at the act, as 322 and 330 refuse). (3) Add a `HaltResponse` frozen value carrying the standing kill instruction the door sent (first-write-wins) and the completed flatten result, so the caller holds the record of both acts. Both values are validated in `__post_init__` rather than only where built, for the reason the channel's and flatten's records do the same: the value is the proof, and a record that could be constructed disagreeing with the acts would launder a residue into a completed halt.

Phase 2 — the endpoint. In `packages/risk/src/risk/halt.py`, add a `HaltEndpoint` class: constructed with the kill switch and flattener it drives (duck-checked against the `send` / `flatten` seams, not isinstance-guarded, because the composed objects are structurally the right shape but never the same class object a direct import yields); carrying `route = RISK_HALT_ROUTE` as a class attribute; with a `from_env` classmethod that resolves both the switch and the flattener from DATABASE_URL exactly as the member's own builders do (returning `None` when nothing names a store — an unconfigured store is a discoverable state, not an error); and with the one verb, `post(request)`, which drives the two acts in order: send the kill (`self._switch.send()`, first-write-wins) then flatten the book (`self._flattener.flatten(request.execution_engine)`, engine-judged completion), returning a `HaltResponse` carrying the standing instruction and the completed flatten result. The kill's and flatten's own refusals propagate unchanged; the endpoint composes no message and performs no store write of its own — the flatten's only store touch is the read of the channel, which is the whole of the hung-proofness.

Phase 3 — the component and the seat. In the member's `__init__.py`, register the endpoint under a fourth component name, `HALT_COMPONENT_NAME = "risk-halt"`, with a `build_risk_halt` builder that resolves the switch and flattener and returns `None` when nothing names a store (degrade-don't-break), following the ledger member's precedent for registering an endpoint beside its store. Re-export `HaltEndpoint`, `HaltRequest`, `HaltResponse` and `RISK_HALT_ROUTE` from the member's `__init__` alongside the existing names. In the seat `src/app/modules/risk/__init__.py`, add one accessor, `halt_component(app=None)`, reached the same way as the existing three (`ledger_component`, `debit_component`, `k_effective_component`), which reads the `risk-halt` component from the composed application.

Phase 4 — the tests. Add one test module, `packages/risk/tests/test_halt.py`, asserting: the endpoint sends the kill then flattens in that order (the standing instruction is on record after `post`, and the book is flat — the engine reports nothing standing); a halt over an already-killed channel writes nothing and returns the first kill's record (`changed=False`) while still flattening; the rejection of new order submission is the consequence — after `post`, `risk.require_orders_allowed` over the same store raises `RiskOrdersKilledError`; the response carries the standing instruction and the completed flatten result (what was cancelled and closed); a flatten that cannot complete (a residue, an engine fault) propagates `RiskFlattenError` and the kill still stands; the endpoint holds no caller-supplied kill moment or sender label (both default to the instant and the kernel-read identity); `HaltEndpoint.from_env` returns `None` when nothing names a store; the endpoint is duck-checked, not isinstance-guarded; and the member's existing three components and all existing risk tests are preserved (feature 323 adds names, it does not remove or reword any). The cross-process case is proven against an actual second interpreter, as the channel's and ledger's suites do: a halt a separate supervisor process pronounces is a kill the order layer's guard refuses under.

Phase 5 — verify. Run the risk member's own suite (`uv run pytest packages/risk/tests`) and the repository-level suite (`uv run pytest tests/`) — both, since the member suite is not graded by the bare gate — and confirm all pass. Lint only the changed files against a sibling (the repo lint is red on main). Confirm no new table was added (the schema is the channel's `risk_order_kill` and nothing else), that exactly one new component is registered (`risk-halt`, beside the existing three), that the seat accessor reaches it, and that no order-sensitive shared file was edited.
